a.summary: The new javadoc mis-scopes the defect as a field-order rule; the real limitation is that any unrecognized field also aborts the import, so the documented workaround does not save a valid config.
a.failure_scenario: A user follows the javadoc — "Put `encoding` first to import the object" — and writes {"encoding":"base58PrivateKey","secret":"BbMQ…KeSb","note":"hot wallet"}. encoding precedes secret exactly as instructed, yet fromJsonPrivateKey still throws JsonException: `testObject: expected [,{}n], but found: ", offset: 95, context: …ret":"BbMQkQYZspmkytduTWvXEtc4mMURjsekJDvty2WtKeSb","note":"»hot wallet"}`. The advertised workaround silently does not work, and the user has no way to derive the real rule from the declaration.

b.summary: The new javadoc's documented workaround ("Put `encoding` first to import the object") is not sufficient — any field name other than pubKey/encoding/secret also aborts the import — and the new test that hits this misattributes the cause in its name.
b.failure_scenario: PrivateKeyEncoding.fromJsonPrivateKey(JsonIterator.parse("{\"encoding\":\"base64PrivateKey\",\"secret\":\"<base64 seed>\",\"note\":\"backup\"}")) follows the documented workaround exactly — encoding precedes secret — and still throws JsonException ("testObject: expected [,{}n], but found: \"") instead of returning the Signer. A consumer reading the new declaration doc will conclude field order is the only limitation and ship a config file with one extra key.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
